description: The HISDAC-ES research team publishes Python scripts that reconstruct historical settlement layers for Spain from cadastral building footprints and attributes. The workflow produces 100 metre raster surfaces in five-year intervals over 1900–2020 using NumPy, SciPy, GDAL and GeoPandas. Separate scripts aggregate building centroids to municipalities, write CSV and GeoPackage statistics, and accelerate residential-building rasterization. GitHub documents the execution roles, while Zenodo archives release_v2. The archive is free and states an other-open licence, but neither the inspected README nor GitHub metadata identifies precise licence terms. These tools can prepare building-stock exposure and settlement-demand inputs for infrastructure simulations, complementing the published HISDAC-ES grids. The August 2023 update corrects earlier rasterization errors and introduces a faster country-wide method that consumes more memory. Original cadastral inputs, paths and software dependencies must be arranged before reuse. No scripts were executed and numerical reproducibility was not checked.
